questions.stem: Q1. A 45-year-old patient is scheduled for an MRI of the brain to assess potential lesions. Which of the following best describes the fundamental principle of MRI?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. A 45-year-old patient is scheduled for an MRI of the brain to assess potential lesions. Which of the following best describes the fundamental principle of MRI?

options.label: A
options.text: Evaluate changes in magnetic field strength around tissues

options.label: B
options.text: Alignment and relaxation of hydrogen nuclei

options.label: C
options.text: Detection of thermal radiation emitted by tissues.

options.label: D
options.text: Measurement of varying ionizing radiation absorption.

questions.stem: Q1. What is the primary difference between axial and helical CT scanning?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. What is the primary difference between axial and helical CT scanning?

options.label: A
options.text: Axial CT uses contrast agents, while helical CT does not.

options.label: B
options.text: Axial CT scans in single slices, while helical CT scans continuously in a spiral.

options.label: C
options.text: Helical CT requires more radiation than axial CT.

options.label: D
options.text: Axial CT produces 3D images, while helical CT produces 2D images.

questions.stem: Q1. A 45-year-old male patient presents with dyspnea on exertion and occasional palpitations. A chest X-ray is performed, revealing the cardiac silhouette. Study the image provided and answer the following question. Which of the following statements regarding the heart's position, size, and borders on the chest radiograph is correct?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. A 45-year-old male patient presents with dyspnea on exertion and occasional palpitations. A chest X-ray is performed, revealing the cardiac silhouette. Study the image provided and answer the following question. Which of the following statements regarding the heart's position, size, and borders on the chest radiograph is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The right heart border is formed primarily by the right ventricle.

options.label: B
options.text: The left atrium primarily forms the left heart border.

options.label: C
options.text: The cardiothoracic ratio (CTR) is considered normal if it is less than 0.5 on a PA chest X-ray.

options.label: D
options.text: The right atrium and the left ventricle mainly form the inferior border of the heart.
